questions.question: Which of the following is NOT continuous data?
questions.answer: Counting gives discrete data (whole numbers only); distance, mass and height are measured, so they are continuous. **(B)**
options: The distance travelled during a trip.
The number of students in a classroom.

questions.question: Linda earns \$980 for one holiday week, which includes $17.5\%$ holiday loading. Which is the correct expression for one week's normal pay?
questions.answer: Pay with loading $= 1.175 \times$ normal pay, so normal pay $= 980 \div 1.175$. **(D)**

questions.question: A company is designing a vinyl wrap to cover the curved surface of a cylindrical drink bottle. The bottle has a diameter of 10 cm and a height of 18 cm. What is the area of vinyl required to cover the curved surface only (no top or base)?
questions.answer: Curved surface $= 2\pi r h = \pi d h = \pi(10)(18) \approx 565\text{ cm}^2$. **(C)**

questions.question: Alex is paid an ordinary hourly rate of \$22.40 before tax. From Monday to Friday, he works 18 hours at the ordinary rate. On Saturday, he works 5 hours paid at time-and-a-half, and on Sunday he works 4 hours paid at double time. Alex's total pay (before tax) for the week is:
Light travels at a speed of $3.0 \times 10^8$ metres per second. How many kilometres does light travel in 36 hours, correct to 2 significant figures?
A group of 150 students completed a short Mathematics quiz. The cumulative frequency graph of their scores is shown. Which of the following identifies the median and mode of the students' scores?
questions.answer:
Cumulative frequencies are 30, 80, 120, 140, 150, so the frequencies for scores 1 to 5 are 30, 50, 40, 20, 10.
- **Median:** the 75th/76th scores lie in the score-2 group (31st to 80th), so the median is 2.
- **Mode:** the most frequent score is 2 (frequency 50).

**(A)**

questions.question: A new law is proposed in NSW and a survey of 1200 people is conducted. Of the 1200 people surveyed, 672 confirmed that they were in favour of this proposed law. Based on this survey, approximately how many of the 1 480 000 voters from this state are expected to vote in favour of this new law?
On a farm, the ratio of dogs to cows to sheep is $2 : 9 : 14$. If the total number of dogs and cows is 33, how many more sheep than cows are on this farm?
questions.answer: Dogs and cows are $2 + 9 = 11$ parts $= 33$, so 1 part $= 3$. Sheep minus cows $= (14 - 9) \times 3 = 15$. **(B)**

questions.question: In a household of 5 people, each person uses a 1500 W electric kettle for an average of 12 minutes every day. The cost of electricity is 37.15 cents per kWh when the kettle is being used. What is the cost of the electricity used by this kettle in 10 weeks?
questions.answer:
Time used $= 5 \times 12 \times 70 = 4200$ min $= 70$ h. Energy $= 1.5 \text{ kW} \times 70 \text{ h} = 105$ kWh.
Cost $= 105 \times 0.3715 = \$39.01$. **(B)**

questions.question: The graphs of four linear equations are shown. Which pair of simultaneous linear equations has the solution $(1, 3)$?
questions.answer: Check which lines pass through $(1, 3)$: $y = 2x + 1$ gives $3$ ✓ and $y = 4 - x$ gives $3$ ✓. The other lines give $y = -3$ ($-2x - 1$), $-2.5$ ($\frac12 x - 3$) and $-1$ ($-2x + 1$) at $x = 1$. **(C)**

questions.question: The graph shows the value of three different annuities over time. Which of the following statements gives a plausible explanation for the different values after seven terms?
questions.answer: All three annuities start at the same value (about \$500) and have the same number of terms, so the starting value and term length cannot explain the gap. Annuity 1 grows most, then 2, then 3, which is consistent with larger regular deposits (or a higher interest rate) for Annuity 1, then 2, then 3. Only **(D)** is a plausible explanation.
options: Annuity 2 and Annuity 3 have higher interest rates than Annuity 1.
Annuity 2 and Annuity 3 have a lower initial value than Annuity 1.
Annuity 1 and Annuity 2 have shorter interest terms than Annuity 3.
Annuity 1 and Annuity 2 have higher regular deposits than Annuity 3.

questions.question: A \$15 000 commercial oven was purchased for a school's hospitality kitchen. After 3 years, its value is \$10 935. The oven depreciates using the declining balance method. What is the annual rate of depreciation, correct to the nearest whole percentage?

$B$ boxes of nails in a factory were inspected and found to be normally distributed with a mean of $r$ nails. The probability that a box had between $r + k$ and $r + 2k$ nails was $9\%$. The probability that a box had between $r - 2k$ and $r + 2k$ nails was $54\%$. Given that 5508 boxes were inspected to have more than $r - k$ nails, how many boxes inspected had more than $r + k$ nails?
The vertices $O$, $A$ and $B$ of an equilateral triangle represent three bus stops. The bearing of $A$ from $O$ is $330^\circ$. Which of the following could be the bearing of $B$ from $A$?
questions.answer: The bearing of $O$ from $A$ is $330^\circ - 180^\circ = 150^\circ$. $B$ lies $60^\circ$ either side of the line $AO$, so the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $150^\circ + 60^\circ = 210^\circ$ or $150^\circ - 60^\circ = 090^\circ$. Only $210^\circ$ is offered. **(C)**

questions.question: Kayne and Aria leave from the same location at the same time and jog in the same direction. If Kayne jogs at an average speed of 10 km/h and Aria at 7 km/h, calculate how far Aria is behind Kayne after 40 minutes.
questions.answer:
Aria falls behind at $10 - 7 = 3$ km/h. In $40$ min $= \frac23$ h:
$$d = 3 \times \tfrac23 = 2\text{ km}$$
Aria is **2 km** behind.

questions.question:
Solve the following equation:
$$\frac{4x - 7}{6} + 2 = \frac{9 - 3x}{4}$$
questions.answer:
Multiply every term by the common denominator 12:
$$2(4x - 7) + 24 = 3(9 - 3x)$$
$$8x + 10 = 27 - 9x \Rightarrow 17x = 17 \Rightarrow x = 1$$
Check: LHS $= \frac{-3}{6} + 2 = 1.5$; RHS $= \frac64 = 1.5$ ✓.

questions.question:
The mass in grams of eight Granny Smith apples picked off a tree are shown.

161, 179, 183, 186, 189, 193, 197, 207

Would the mass of the lightest apple be considered to be an outlier? Justify your answer with calculations.
questions.answer:
$Q_1 = \frac{179 + 183}{2} = 181$, $Q_3 = \frac{193 + 197}{2} = 195$, so $\text{IQR} = 195 - 181 = 14$.

Lower fence $= Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 181 - 21 = 160$.

The lightest apple (161 g) is above 160 g, so it is **not** an outlier.

questions.question:
Emily looked at her receipt for groceries from the supermarket and noted that she had paid GST of $10\%$ on some items she bought, and no GST on other items. Emily paid a total of \$35.33 for her groceries including GST. The only item she bought that was GST-free was a bunch of grapes for \$7.94. The items she bought that included GST were chocolate for \$9.00, a frozen pizza for \$7.50 and some cat litter.

What was the total amount of GST that Emily paid?
questions.answer:
The items with GST cost $35.33 - 7.94 = \$27.39$ in total (price already includes GST, which is $\frac{1}{11}$ of it):
$$\text{GST} = \frac{27.39}{11} = \$2.49$$

questions.question: A company has decided to distribute \$63 million of its profits as dividends. The company has issued 210 million shares, and each share is valued at \$174.62. Calculate the dividend yield (as a percentage) of each share to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
Dividend per share $= \dfrac{63}{210} = \$0.30$.
$$\text{Yield} = \frac{0.30}{174.62} \times 100\% \approx 0.17\%$$
(The school's working contains a slip but reaches the same value, $0.17\%$.)

questions.question:
Susan travels from city $P$ (UTC $-7$) to city $Q$ (UTC $-3$). The flight between these two cities took 6 hours. The flight arrived at city $Q$ at 3:30 a.m. local time on Thursday the 4th of October.

On what day and what time did Susan's flight leave city $P$ for this journey?
questions.answer:
City $Q$ is $4$ hours ahead of city $P$.
- Departure in $Q$'s time: $3{:}30\text{ am} - 6\text{ h} = 9{:}30\text{ pm}$ on Wednesday 3 October.
- Convert to $P$'s time: $9{:}30\text{ pm} - 4\text{ h} = 5{:}30\text{ pm}$.

The flight left city $P$ at **5:30 pm on Wednesday 3 October**.

questions.question:
Jenny weighs 74 kg. She ate 143 g of trout and 48 g of noodles. The labels on these products indicate that the trout has 220 kJ of energy in a 55 g serve, and the noodles has 1020 kJ in a 120 g serve.

Calculate the number of kJ in her trout and noodles.
questions.answer:
Trout: $\frac{143}{55} \times 220 = 572$ kJ. Noodles: $\frac{48}{120} \times 1020 = 408$ kJ.

Total $= 572 + 408 = 980$ kJ.

questions.question:
Jenny weighs 74 kg. She ate 143 g of trout and 48 g of noodles. The labels on these products indicate that the trout has 220 kJ of energy in a 55 g serve, and the noodles has 1020 kJ in a 120 g serve.

The table below shows the number of kilocalories used each minute in a variety of exercises for different body masses. 1 kilocalorie is equivalent to 4.184 kilojoules.

| Activity | 56 kg | 62 kg | 74 kg |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volleyball | 2.8 | 3.2 | 3.7 |
| Dancing | 7.5 | 9.5 | 10.0 |
| Tennis | 6.1 | 7.8 | 8.1 |

For how many minutes must Jenny play tennis in order to use all the energy in the trout and the noodles? (Answer to the nearest minute.)
questions.answer:
Jenny is 74 kg, so tennis uses $8.1$ kcal/min $= 8.1 \times 4.184 = 33.89$ kJ/min.
$$t = \frac{980}{33.89} \approx 28.9 \approx 29\text{ minutes}$$
(Using the total of 980 kJ from part (a).)

questions.question:
In a game, Joe has three attempts to roll two dice, each with faces numbered 1 to 6. In any attempt she will:
- WIN A PRIZE if the sum of the topmost faces is at least 8.
- TRY AGAIN if the sum of the topmost faces is 5, 6 or 7.
- LOSE if the sum of the topmost faces is 4 or less.

If Joe wins a prize, or loses, the game is over.

Complete the table, using W for win, T for try again and L for lose.
questions.answer:
Each cell is decided by the sum of the two dice.

| 2nd die \ 1st die | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | L | L | L | T | T | T |
| 2 | L | L | T | T | T | W |
| 3 | L | T | T | T | W | W |
| 4 | T | T | T | W | W | W |
| 5 | T | T | W | W | W | W |
| 6 | T | W | W | W | W | W |

There are $15$ W, $15$ T and $6$ L out of $36$ outcomes.

questions.question:
In a game, Joe has three attempts to roll two dice, each with faces numbered 1 to 6. In any attempt she will:
- WIN A PRIZE if the sum of the topmost faces is at least 8.
- TRY AGAIN if the sum of the topmost faces is 5, 6 or 7.
- LOSE if the sum of the topmost faces is 4 or less.

If Joe wins a prize, or loses, the game is over.

Fill in the probabilities in the probability tree below (each attempt has the branches WIN, TRY AGAIN and LOSE).
questions.answer:
From the table: $P(W) = \frac{15}{36} = \frac{5}{12}$, $P(T) = \frac{15}{36} = \frac{5}{12}$, $P(L) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac16$.

The probabilities are the same on every attempt: WIN $\frac{5}{12}$, TRY AGAIN $\frac{5}{12}$, LOSE $\frac16$.

questions.question:
In a game, Joe has three attempts to roll two dice, each with faces numbered 1 to 6. In any attempt she will:
- WIN A PRIZE if the sum of the topmost faces is at least 8.
- TRY AGAIN if the sum of the topmost faces is 5, 6 or 7.
- LOSE if the sum of the topmost faces is 4 or less.

If Joe wins a prize, or loses, the game is over.

What is the probability that Joe wins a prize in this game?
questions.answer:
She wins on the 1st attempt, or tries again then wins on the 2nd, or tries twice then wins on the 3rd:
$$P(\text{win}) = \frac{5}{12} + \frac{5}{12}\cdot\frac{5}{12} + \left(\frac{5}{12}\right)^2\cdot\frac{5}{12} = \frac{5}{12} + \frac{25}{144} + \frac{125}{1728} = \frac{1145}{1728} \approx 66.26\%$$

questions.question:
A new laptop is purchased for \$2450 using a credit card. The credit card has an interest-free period of 55 days from and including the date of purchase. After this period ends, interest is charged on the purchase made, compounding daily at a rate of $15.4\%$ per annum, from and including the day following the interest-free period. The full payment for the laptop is made on the 90th day from the date of purchase. There were no other purchases on this credit card.

What was the total interest charged when the account was paid in full?
questions.answer:
Interest is charged from day 56 to day 90: $90 - 55 = 35$ days. The daily rate is $\frac{15.4\%}{365} = \frac{0.154}{365}$.
$$A = 2450\left(1 + \frac{0.154}{365}\right)^{35} \approx 2486.44$$
$$\text{Interest} = 2486.44 - 2450 \approx \$36.44$$

questions.question:
A shopkeeper notes how much money, $\$A$, customers have spent in the store and how many minutes, $t$, it took them to decide what they wanted to buy. The diagram shows the dataset and a line of best fit.

Find the equation of the line of best fit.
questions.answer:
The line passes through $(0, 40)$ and $(8, 0)$: gradient $m = \frac{0 - 40}{8 - 0} = -5$, vertical intercept $40$.
$$A = -5t + 40$$

questions.question:
A shopkeeper notes how much money, $\$A$, customers have spent in the store and how many minutes, $t$, it took them to decide what they wanted to buy. The diagram shows the dataset and a line of best fit.

Suppose another customer spent \$20 after taking 7 minutes to decide what they wanted to buy. A new line of best fit is created to account for this extra customer. Describe how the gradient of the line of best fit would change from the answer found in part (a).
questions.answer: The point $(7, 20)$ lies well above the current line (which gives $A = 5$ at $t = 7$), so the line is pulled up at the right-hand end. The gradient becomes **less negative** (it increases, closer to zero).

questions.question:
Buntings can be made from individual flags held together with string. The diagram below shows five identical flags on a 1 metre length of string. There is a 1 cm gap between each flag and 8 cm at each end of the string to tie the bunting on display.

The material for one flag consists of two shapes, a rectangle and an equilateral triangle. The diagram shows the shape and dimensions of one flag (the rectangle is 16 cm by 4 cm).

Determine whether or not it is suitable to have six identical flags on the 1 metre length of string. Justify your statement with relevant calculations.
questions.answer:
Six flags need $6 \times 16 = 96$ cm, five 1 cm gaps $= 5$ cm and $2 \times 8 = 16$ cm at the ends:
$$96 + 5 + 16 = 117\text{ cm} > 100\text{ cm}$$
Six flags would not fit, so it is **not suitable**.

questions.question:
Buntings can be made from individual flags held together with string. The diagram below shows five identical flags on a 1 metre length of string. There is a 1 cm gap between each flag and 8 cm at each end of the string to tie the bunting on display.

The material for one flag consists of two shapes, a rectangle and an equilateral triangle. The diagram shows the shape and dimensions of one flag (the rectangle is 16 cm by 4 cm).

Calculate the area of one flag to the nearest 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
Rectangle: $16 \times 4 = 64\text{ cm}^2$.
Equilateral triangle of side 16 cm: $\frac12(16)(16)\sin 60^\circ \approx 110.85\text{ cm}^2$.
$$A \approx 64 + 110.85 = 174.85\text{ cm}^2$$

questions.question:
After a ball is thrown off a building, the height of the ball can be modelled by the equation $h = at^2 + 4t + c$, where $t$ is time in seconds after the ball is thrown off the building, and $h$ is the height of the ball above the ground in metres. The graph shows the height of the ball above the ground after $t$ seconds. Two points, $(0, 16)$ and $(3, 10)$, are also shown on the graph.

Only a part of the graph applies to this model. Find all values of $t$ that are not suitable to use with this model and explain why these values are not suitable.
questions.answer:
The $t$-intercepts are $t = -2$ and $t = 4$.
- $t < 0$ is not suitable: time before the ball was thrown is meaningless.
- $t > 4$ is not suitable: the height would be negative (below the ground), because the ball has already hit the ground at $t = 4$.

| City | Sydney (S) | Coffs Harbour (C) | Orange (O) | Melbourne (M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (S) | – | \$205 | \$231 | \$174 |
| (C) | \$205 | – | – | \$593 |
| (O) | \$231 | – | – | \$499 |

questions.answer:

questions.question:
The network shown in the table below gives the cost of flights between four airports. For example, the cost between Sydney and Coffs Harbour is \$205.

| City | Sydney (S) | Coffs Harbour (C) | Orange (O) | Melbourne (M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (S) | – | \$205 | \$231 | \$174 |
| (C) | \$205 | – | – | \$593 |
| (O) | \$231 | – | – | \$499 |
| (M) | \$174 | \$593 | \$499 | – |

A passenger had to fly from Orange to Coffs Harbour in an emergency. They intended to take the cheapest route, but when they went to book the flights they found that all the Orange to Sydney services had been cancelled for the day. They booked the cheapest route that did NOT include a flight from Orange to Sydney. What was the percentage increase in the cost of their flights due to the cancelled services? Answer as a percentage correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
Cheapest route: $O \to S \to C = 231 + 205 = \$436$.

Without $O$–$S$: $O \to M \to S \to C = 499 + 174 + 205 = \$878$ (the other option $O \to M \to C = \$1092$ is dearer).
$$\text{Increase} = \frac{878 - 436}{436} \times 100\% \approx 101.4\%$$

questions.question:
In the diagram, $AB$ is a road running in the south-east direction, $C$ is an observatory on a bearing of $205^\circ$ from $A$, and $BC = 30$ km. A man travels along the road from $B$ to $A$. After walking 20 km to $D$, he is 21 km from $C$.

Calculate how far the man is from $A$. Give your answer correct to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer:
**Angle $B$** (cosine rule in $\triangle CBD$, $CB = 30$, $BD = 20$, $CD = 21$):
$$\cos B = \frac{30^2 + 20^2 - 21^2}{2(30)(20)} = \frac{859}{1200} \Rightarrow B \approx 44.29^\circ$$
**Angle $A$:** $AB$ runs on bearing $135^\circ$ and $AC$ on bearing $205^\circ$, so $\angle BAC = 205^\circ - 135^\circ = 70^\circ$. Then $\angle C = 180^\circ - 70^\circ - 44.29^\circ = 65.71^\circ$.

**Sine rule in $\triangle ABC$:**
$$AB = \frac{30\sin 65.71^\circ}{\sin 70^\circ} \approx 29.1\text{ km}$$
$$AD = AB - BD \approx 29.1 - 20 \approx 9\text{ km}$$

questions.question:

Identify the direction and strength of the linear association between $M$ and $E$.
questions.answer: $r \approx -0.99$ is close to $-1$: a **strong negative** linear association.

questions.question:
A set of bivariate data was collected by recording the marks students received in a Music quiz, $M$, and an Economics quiz, $E$. In each quiz students gained either 0 marks or 1 mark for each question. The graph shows a scatterplot of these measurements: the points $(1, 8)$, $(3, 5)$ and $(6, 2)$.

Another student was absent for the Economics quiz but achieved 10 marks in the Music quiz. By creating a line of best fit or otherwise, explain why the student's Economics mark could not be estimated using the association between $M$ and $E$ for the other students.
questions.answer: The line of best fit is about $E = -1.2M + 9.2$. A Music mark of 10 is outside the range of the data ($1 \le M \le 6$), so using it is **extrapolation**, which is unreliable. Here it would also give $E \approx -2.8$, an impossible negative mark.

questions.question:
A flu virus spreads in a little town on an island. The number of people $N$ infected $D$ days after the virus started to spread can be modelled by the equation $N = Ka^D$, where $K$ and $a$ are constants. The graph shows the number of people $N$ infected after $D$ days, passing through $(0, 4)$ and $(3, 32)$.

Using the information shown on the graph, find the number of people infected after 10 days.
questions.answer:
At $(0, 4)$: $4 = Ka^0 = K$, so $K = 4$.
At $(3, 32)$: $32 = 4a^3 \Rightarrow a^3 = 8 \Rightarrow a = 2$.

So $N = 4 \times 2^D$ and
$$N(10) = 4 \times 2^{10} = 4096\text{ people}$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows a slide in a fun park. The slide has a curved surface on the top and a uniform cross-sectional area in the front as shown. Also, its left side and its base are rectangular faces. The base is 15.6 m long, the left side is 9.6 m high, and the heights 6.8 m and 3.4 m are measured at equal intervals along the base.

Use three applications of the trapezoidal rule to find an approximate area for the cross section.
questions.answer:
Three strips of width $h = \frac{15.6}{3} = 5.2$ m with heights $9.6,\ 6.8,\ 3.4,\ 0$:
$$A \approx \frac{5.2}{2}\left[9.6 + 2(6.8 + 3.4) + 0\right] = 2.6 \times 30 = 78\text{ m}^2$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows a slide in a fun park. The slide has a curved surface on the top and a uniform cross-sectional area in the front as shown. Also, its left side and its base are rectangular faces. The base is 15.6 m long, the left side is 9.6 m high, and the heights 6.8 m and 3.4 m are measured at equal intervals along the base.

If the curved area on the top is $169.68\text{ m}^2$ and the total surface area of the slide (including the base) is $537.36\text{ m}^2$, what is an approximate value of the width $W$?
questions.answer:
Total surface area $=$ curved top $+$ base $+$ left side $+$ two identical cross-sections:
$$537.36 = 169.68 + 15.6W + 9.6W + 2(78)$$
$$211.68 = 25.2W \Rightarrow W = 8.4\text{ m}$$

questions.question:
Peter placed 15 identical small spherical marbles each of radius 2 cm in a large hemispherical bowl of radius $R$. The volume of the empty space in the bowl is $992\pi\text{ cm}^3$.

What is the radius $R$ of the hemispherical bowl?
questions.answer:
Volume of the 15 marbles $= 15 \times \frac43\pi(2)^3 = 160\pi$.

Volume of the bowl $= \frac23\pi R^3$. Empty space $=$ bowl $-$ marbles:
$$\tfrac23\pi R^3 - 160\pi = 992\pi \Rightarrow \tfrac23 R^3 = 1152 \Rightarrow R^3 = 1728$$
$$R = 12\text{ cm}$$

questions.question:
Water is to be pumped through a field, from the source at $A$ to the sink at $E$, using a series of pipes from pumping station locations, labelled $A$ to $G$. The network diagram shows the maximum flow rate through each of these pipes, measured in thousands of litres per hour.

What is the capacity of the cut shown in the diagram?
questions.answer:
Add the capacities of the pipes that cross the cut from the source side to the sink side: $BC = 19$ and $FE = 16$ (the pipes $CG$ and $DF$ carry flow back towards the source side, so they are not counted):
$$19 + 16 = 35$$

questions.question:
Water is to be pumped through a field, from the source at $A$ to the sink at $E$, using a series of pipes from pumping station locations, labelled $A$ to $G$. The network diagram shows the maximum flow rate through each of these pipes, measured in thousands of litres per hour.

Calculate the maximum flow of this network.
questions.answer:
The maximum flow equals the minimum cut. The cut through $CD$ and $GF$ has capacity $15 + 10 = 25$, and no other cut is smaller.

Maximum flow $= 25$ thousand litres per hour.

questions.question:
Water is to be pumped through a field, from the source at $A$ to the sink at $E$, using a series of pipes from pumping station locations, labelled $A$ to $G$. The network diagram shows the maximum flow rate through each of these pipes, measured in thousands of litres per hour.

The owners of this field want to increase the flow of water through one of the pipes in order to increase the maximum flow of this network. Which pipe should they choose, and what is the minimum amount by which its flow should be increased in order to maximise the amount of water flowing through this network?
questions.answer:
The minimum cut ($CD$ and $GF$, capacity 25) must be raised, so the pipe to increase is $CD$ or $GF$.
- **Increase $CD$:** the cut $AB + GF = 16 + 10 = 26$ then limits the flow to 26, so the gain is only 1.
- **Increase $GF$ by $x$:** the minimum cut becomes $CD + GF = 25 + x$, until it reaches the next smallest cut, $CD + FE = 15 + 16 = 31$.

Choose pipe **$GF$** and increase it by **6** thousand litres per hour, giving a maximum flow of $31$ thousand litres per hour.

questions.question:
The activity table shows the tasks required to complete a construction project.

| Activity | Prerequisite/s | Duration (days) |
|---|---|---|
| A | – | 4 |
| B | A | 6 |
| C | A | 5 |
| D | B, C | 3 |
| E | C | 4 |
| F | D, E | 2 |

Activity $C$ is delayed by two days. Determine the new critical path to describe how this delay affects the project's completion time. Construct a network diagram to support your answer.
questions.answer:
**Original:** the longest path is $A$–$B$–$D$–$F$ $= 4 + 6 + 3 + 2 = 15$ days (the path $A$–$C$–$E$–$F$ is $4 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 15$ days as well, and $A$–$C$–$D$–$F$ is $14$).

**After the delay** ($C$ now takes $7$ days): $A$–$C$–$E$–$F$ $= 4 + 7 + 4 + 2 = 17$ days and $A$–$C$–$D$–$F$ $= 16$ days, so these are now longer than $A$–$B$–$D$–$F$ $= 15$.

The new critical path is **$A$–$C$–$E$–$F$**, and the minimum completion time increases from 15 days to **17 days**: the delay of 2 days in $C$ delays the whole project by 2 days. The network diagram (earliest and latest start times in boxes, with a dummy activity from $B$ to the start of $D$) is shown in the answer image.

questions.question:
The table shows the percentage of scores which lie between $z = 0$ and $z = a$, where $a$ is a positive value, for a normal distribution. Symmetry properties of the distribution can be used to determine other percentages.

The ages (in years) of the members of the Martin Bay Tennis Club are normally distributed with a mean of 32 and a standard deviation of 16.0.

Convert an age of 48 to a $z$-score.

The table shows the percentage of scores which lie between $z = 0$ and $z = a$, where $a$ is a positive value, for a normal distribution. Symmetry properties of the distribution can be used to determine other percentages.

The ages (in years) of the members of the Martin Bay Tennis Club are normally distributed with a mean of 32 and a standard deviation of 16.0.

What percentage of the members are aged less than 48? Answer as a whole percentage.
questions.answer:
$z = 1$ gives $34.13\%$ between the mean and $48$, plus $50\%$ below the mean:
$$50 + 34.13 = 84.13\% \approx 84\%$$

The tables show the future values and present values of annuities of \$1 for a variety of periods and interest rates. Contributions are made at the end of each period.

Jane invested \$3500 at the end of each year for 12 years into an annuity with an interest rate of 9% per annum. After 5 years, she decided to invest in an additional annuity at 6% per annum, making equal annual contributions at the end of each year for the next 7 years. She wants the total value of both annuities after 12 years to be \$100 000.

To fund the annual contributions to the second annuity, Jane borrows each contribution amount at an interest rate of 6% per annum and repays it in 12 equal monthly instalments over the following year.

Calculate the amount Jane must pay back each month for the contributions to the additional annuity.
questions.answer:
**First annuity** (12 years, 9%, factor $20.141$): $3500 \times 20.141 = \$70\,493.50$.

**Second annuity** must provide $100\,000 - 70\,493.50 = \$29\,506.50$. Over 7 years at 6% the future value factor is $8.394$:
$$C = \frac{29\,506.50}{8.394} = \$3515.19$$
**Monthly repayments:** borrowing $C$ at 6% p.a. $= 0.5\%$ per month for 12 months, the present value factor is $11.619$:
$$\text{Instalment} = \frac{3515.19}{11.619} \approx \$302.54\text{ per month}$$
